Team news & overrides — this gameweek only

Overrides apply only to the gameweek you're viewing above — a player ruled out for GW3 still shows normal predictions for GW4 onward.
Bench Boost
Points from your bench are only useful when your bench itself has a strong week. Bar height = simulated expected bench contribution; amber = the strongest week in this horizon.
Triple Captain
Best single (player, gameweek) combination in your squad by simulated ceiling — the ordinary captain choice maximizes the mean, this looks at upside specifically.
Wildcard / Free Hit timing
Your squad's simulated total across the horizon. A gameweek sitting well below your own average is where a squad overhaul earns its cost back fastest.

Transfer suggestions

Ranked as a sequence: each suggestion is checked against your budget and squad after the ones before it, so if you take them in order the combination is always affordable — it won't suggest transfers that are only affordable individually but not together. Still a greedy heuristic (best single swap at each step), not a true multi-transfer optimizer — it won't find a pair of transfers that only pays off together.

Transfer timing plan

The list above answers which swaps are worth making. This answers when — solved exactly by dynamic programming over free-transfer banking, hit costs and wildcard use, rather than the greedy "act every week" assumption. It schedules the shortlist above optimally; it does not discover new targets that only become affordable after an earlier move.

Value screen

Moneyball-style screen: compares each player's total predicted points over the horizon against their cost AND their effective ownership - looking for players the MODEL rates well that the CROWD hasn't priced in yet (low EO), not just cheap players. "Pts/£m" alone favours cheap enablers regardless of ownership; "Differential score" specifically rewards being right where the field isn't. Horizon totals are decay-weighted (0.95/GW) - a GW15 prediction is inherently less reliable than GW1, so it counts for less rather than being treated as equally certain. Requires effective_ownership.py to have been run for the EO half of this - without it, everything still ranks by raw value.

Rotation pairs

Finds pairs of players whose fixture runs complement each other — when one is away at a title contender, the other is home to a promoted side. You own both and start whichever has the better fixture that week.

Rotation gain is the honest measure: how many points the PAIR earns over the horizon versus simply playing the better of the two every week. A high total with a LOW gain means one player is just better and you don't need the other. A high gain means the fixtures genuinely alternate, which is the whole point.

Pairs are never drawn from the same club (identical fixtures = zero rotation value). Assumes you pick correctly each week, which gets harder further out — treat distant gameweeks as indicative.
Predictions come from a decay-weighted Poisson team model (backtested half-life 1.5 seasons) and a per-player expected-points estimate blending 2025/26 season rates (or discounted Championship rates for Coventry/Hull/ Ipswich) with fixture strength. Involvement probability is a season-average proxy, not live team news — that's what the overrides panel is for. Simulations use 3,000 Monte Carlo draws per player-gameweek from the same underlying rates as the point estimate, so means match exactly; only the spread is new information. Transfer suggestions are a greedy single-swap heuristic, not a guaranteed-optimal multi-transfer plan.
